definition: Orange is an open-source data visualization, machine learning and data mining toolkit.
details: It features a visual programming front-end for exploratory qualitative data analysis and interactive data visualization.

explainer.lead: Orange is an open-source toolkit for exploring data, building machine-learning workflows, and mining data through a visual interface. It lets people combine analysis and interactive visualization without making programming the center of the experience.

tiers.eli5: Orange is like a set of building blocks for exploring information. You connect blocks that work with data and look at colorful, interactive pictures of the results, which can help you notice groups or patterns.
tiers.practitioner: Orange is used to assemble data-mining and machine-learning experiments visually while inspecting results through interactive plots. It suits exploratory analysis and rapid workflow iteration, but an easy-to-build workflow still needs careful data preparation and model evaluation.
tiers.paperLevel: Orange is an open-source software toolkit integrating data visualization, machine learning, and data mining through a visual-programming front-end. Its interaction model supports exploratory qualitative data analysis and interactive visualization rather than defining a single algorithm or formal objective.

explainer.example: A user loads a table of flower measurements, connects a classification workflow to an interactive visualization, and examines which flowers are grouped incorrectly before changing the analysis.

usedIn.name: Exploratory data analysis
usedIn.detail: Building visual workflows for qualitative investigation of a dataset.

usedIn.name: Interactive data visualization
usedIn.detail: Examining data and analysis results through interactive visual views.

usedIn.name: Machine-learning prototyping
usedIn.detail: Combining machine-learning and data-mining steps without centering the work on handwritten code.

explainer.intuition: Orange turns data analysis into a visible workflow: instead of treating exploration, visualization, and machine learning as separate activities, you connect them and inspect what happens.
howItWorks: Bring a dataset into the visual workspace.
Connect data-mining or machine-learning steps into a workflow.
Use interactive visualizations to inspect the data and results.
Adjust the workflow as patterns or problems become visible.
explainer.whyItMatters: A visual front-end can make exploratory analysis more approachable and keep results visible while a workflow is being developed. This is useful when understanding the data interactively matters as much as producing a final model.
misconceptions: Orange is not a single machine-learning algorithm; it is a toolkit.
It is not only for making charts: it also supports machine learning and data mining.
A visual workflow does not remove the need to check data quality and evaluation choices.

diagram.caption: Orange connects data, analysis, and interactive visualization in an exploratory loop.
